caption:
सलमान खान की फिल्म Maatrubhumi का 4 मिनट 35 सेकंड का ट्रेलर आखिरकार सामने आ गया है! 🎬
यह फिल्म साल 2020 की गलवान घाटी की झड़प से प्रेरित है और 16 बिहार रेजिमेंट के इर्द-गिर्द घूमती है।
मेकर्स का दावा है कि फिल्म का फोकस युद्ध की इंसानी कीमत और बॉर्डर पार यूनिवर्सल शांति पर है। 🇮🇳
लेकिन ट्रेलर में सलमान खान का 'Shezwan mein kuch kaala hai' जैसा मॉडर्न स्लैंग बोलना काफी अजीब लगता है।
सलमान खान ने एक बिहारी फौजी का किरदार निभाया है, पर उनका स्क्रीन प्रेजेंस एक आर्मी कमांडर जैसा कम और खुद सलमान खान जैसा ज्यादा लगता है। 🪖
चित्रांगदा सिंह ने भी इसमें एक इमोशनल एंगल देने की कोशिश की है, जो घर पर परिवार का इंतजार दिखाने वाला एक टिपिकल रोल लगता है।
डायरेक्टर अपूर्वा लाखिया फिल्म में सही बैलेंस बनाने के लिए संघर्ष करते दिखते हैं, जहाँ फाइट सीक्वेंस और लाउड बैकग्राउंड स्कोर में गहराई की कमी खलती है। ⚡
क्या आपको लगता है कि सलमान खान की यह फिल्म बॉक्स ऑफिस पर कमाल कर पाएगी? 🍿

ctx.title: Maatrubhumi Trailer Review: Salman Khan Playing A Bihari Was Not On My List Ever – One Thing I Agree – This Film Will Be A Battle!
ctx.summary:
Maatrubhumi trailer is finally out and I just want to know, exactly who will tell Salman Khan that Bhai, it's done bro - trailer review! 
 The post  Maatrubhumi Trailer Review: Salman Khan Playing A Bihari Was Not On My List Ever – One Thing I Agree – This Film Will Be A Battle!  appeared first on  Koimoi .
ctx.text:
Inspired by the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and loosely adapting chapters around the 16 Bihar Regiment, Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace (formerly titled Battle of Galwan) had every ingredient to deliver a raw and deeply respectful war cinema experience. The film has been waiting for a long time, and I feel it wasn’t for the best, because the trailer does not do anything that proves it was worth the wait!
Instead, the 4-minute 35-second trailer reveals a script that seems to be having a massive identity crisis. On one hand, the makers claim to focus on the human cost of war and preach universal peace across borders. On the other hand, the writing seems to be heavily restrained.
Watching a Bollywood superstar confront opposing troops on a frozen riverbank only to drop modern slang like Shezwan mein kuch kaala hai is completely a disgrace, to be honest! Rather than capturing the grim, silent valor of real soldiers fighting in sub-zero temperatures, the trailer plays out like a glossy, over-dramatized TV saga where subtlety goes to die.
Salman Khan steps into the boots of a soldier who hails from Bihar, but his screen presence is burdened by a lack of authentic characterization. Instead of disappearing into the discipline of an Indian Army Commander, it feels like Salman Khan playing Salman Khan in uniform. His attempt to channel a Bihari war cry comes across as forced, while his anti-war monologues sound like speeches meant for anywhere else rather than a military bunker.
Chitrangda Singh provides a brief emotional anchor, but her sub-plot already feels like a textbook-checked role designed solely to check the family waiting back home box.
Director Apoorva Lakhia , who has previously helmed action flicks like Shootout at Lokhandwala, seems to struggle to find a balance with Maatrubhumi. The fight sequences lack sharp choreography; the loud background score lacks genuine tension.
The trailer for Maatrubhumi fails to spark genuine excitement or honor its heavy subject matter with the nuance it deserved. Two things are for sure – Watching Salman Khan play a Bihari will be a task, and this film will be a battle in itself!
